steps.title: Install and grant access
steps.body: Verify the package, install it with your package manager, then run sudo vault443-access "$USER" once from your normal desktop user's terminal.

steps.title: Bring a profile
steps.body: Open Vault 443 from the application launcher. Import a supported link or file, or add an HTTPS subscription. Your server or subscription comes from you.

faq.heading: A few things before you connect.

items.question: Does Vault 443 provide VPN servers?
items.answer: Vault 443 is a client for your own server configurations or subscriptions. It does not provide a VPN service or require a Vault 443 account.

items.question: Which profiles can I import?
items.answer: Supported VLESS, Trojan and Shadowsocks/Outline links, files and subscriptions; self-contained certificate-based OpenVPN TUN profiles; WireGuard and AmneziaWG client configurations; autonomous Amnezia vpn:// exports. OpenVPN passwords, MFA/SSO, encrypted private keys, TAP and user scripts/plugins are unsupported.

items.question: Does the interface need root?
items.answer: The interface runs as your regular user in an active local desktop session. An administrator grants access once with vault443-access. A separate system service handles networking. Do not launch the GUI with sudo.

items.question: Can work VPNs run alongside my internet connection?
items.answer: Work VPNs with specific work routes can run alongside the main connection. A verified full-tunnel work VPN pauses the main connection until its routes are released. Work profiles start manually after reboot.

items.question: How do I update or uninstall?
items.answer: Verify the new package and repeat your distribution's install command. Use apt remove vault443, dnf remove vault443 or pacman -R vault443 to uninstall. Normal removal releases Vault 443's network resources and retains private profiles in /var/lib/vault443.

items.question: What happens when the tunnel fails?
items.answer: The network guard blocks direct internet traffic while the connection recovers, including forwarded Docker bridge traffic. An explicit Disconnect releases protection. If the service cannot recover, the documentation explains how to release the network safely.

windows.heading: Your console for Windows.
windows.requirements: Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11, x64. Setup includes Qt, VPN engines, runtime libraries and official Wintun.
windows.unsigned: The EXE and installer are not Authenticode-signed. Vault 443 is publisher metadata, not a verified UAC publisher.
windows.verify: Download the EXE and its .sha256 file. Run the PowerShell command and compare its hash with the checksum file.
windows.install: Run setup from your regular session, approve UAC and choose a local disk and folder. Then open Vault 443 from the Start menu and add a profile.

steps.title: Install for Windows
steps.body: Verify SHA-256, run the EXE from your regular session and approve UAC. Choose a local disk and folder. The installer includes the required components.

steps.title: Bring a profile
steps.body: Open Vault 443 from the Start menu. Import a supported link or file, or add an HTTPS subscription. Bring your own server or subscription.

steps.title: Connect and stay informed

privileges.question: Windows: do I need administrator rights?
privileges.answer: Run setup from your regular user session and approve UAC. Setup installs the system service and grants the current user access. The window runs as a regular user. Administrative actions can request UAC.

update.question: Windows: how do I update or uninstall?
update.answer: Verify the new EXE and run it over the installed version. The installation folder, profiles and settings are retained. Uninstall through Windows Settings → Apps. To move folders, uninstall and reinstall; profiles and logs in %ProgramData%\Vault443 are retained by default.

recovery.question: Windows: what happens when the tunnel fails?
recovery.answer: The network guard blocks direct internet traffic during recovery. An explicit Disconnect releases protection. If the service fails to start after an update, rerun the verified installer. See the Windows guide for further recovery steps.
